title: Adaptive micro-fragmentation layout for multi-GPU KV cache in tensor+pipeline interop
creator: Maya R. Patel
description:
Problem statement: As we run production streaming workloads with continuous batching, KV cache residency and layout across tensor- and pipeline-parallel boundaries is the dominant source of extra GPU memory consumption and uneven latency spikes. Existing slab or stripe sharding allocates large contiguous KV slabs per-GPU which leads to hot-key concentration, imbalanced memory pressure, and expensive cross-device transfers when pipeline stages move token ownership.

Goal: Design and implement an adaptive micro-fragmentation layout that breaks KV cache slabs into small fragments (micro-fragments) and provides placement, ownership, and coalescing policies that optimize for: (1) memory packing across heterogeneous GPU topologies, (2) low tail latency under continuous batching, and (3) minimal cross-device synchronization during pipeline handoffs. The implementation should be compatible with our serving runtime, support live rollouts, and include observability for fragment hotness and fragmentation overhead.

Scope and constraints: Focus on inference-only KV caches (no training), preserve KV lookup semantics and correctness, and keep the runtime CPU overhead within our current scheduling budget (<2% of token-level cost). Support tensor-parallel (TP) sharded model partitions and pipeline-parallel (PP) stage boundaries; support heterogeneous device memory sizes and NVLink/PCIe bandwidth differences.

Deliverables: design doc with algorithm and data structures, prototype runtime changes (placement map + fast coalescer), microbench harness, performance regression tests, migration / fallback policy, and canary rollout on Dedicated capacity.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end KV correctness preserved for TP+PP models (unit tests pass)
Memory overhead reduction >= 20% vs current slab sharding under mixed-length streams in synthetic benchmark
P50 latency improved or equal and P99 not regressing by more than 5% on chat-like workload with continuous batching
Runtime CPU overhead for placement/coalescing < 2% tokens cost in perf profile
Canary rollout plan and automated fallback that can revert to existing slab sharding without state loss
comments: 2026-03-02 - JR: Initial spike profiling shows KV resident ratio variance of up to 38% across GPUs for a 16‑beam chat workload. Captured traces uploaded to perf dashboard.
2026-03-05 - MP: Design review held with runtime and infra. Decided on a placement map + fragment ownership table to avoid heavyweight distributed locks. Julian to prototype map layout.

2026-03-08 - JR: Prototype implemented: micro-fragments of 64KB with per-fragment 'hot-score' counters. Early synthetic tests show 12-18% memory compaction and 6% p50 improvement under steady batches.
2026-03-10 - DS (infra): Noted NVLink topology impacts: fragments should prefer NVLink-local GPUs for coalescing; added topology-aware preference in placement heuristic.
2026-03-12 - JR: Observed increased CPU cycles for coalescer under pathological churn. Added lightweight rate limiter and background coalescing worker to amortize cost.
2026-03-14 - MP: Need to define migration semantics when rolling back to slab mode. Action: add dependent migration tool to export/import fragment map to slab mapping (ENG-220421).
